templates.name: Transformation

templates.finish: Merge the target state into the current state when it is reached (Finish › merge into its parent).

templates.name: Risk and security architecture
templates.description: When what is at risk, and how it is protected, must be known: an audit finding, a regulation, a breach, a security review. Phase by phase: risk appetite and business impact in Preliminary, security in the vision, the risk assessment and register in B, classification in C, the security of the technology in D, the mitigation plan in E and F, audit and the residual risk signed off in G, changes in risk handled in H, the security requirements in Requirements Management.

slots.label: Current state
slots.help: The architecture as it is, and its risks today.

slots.label: Target state
slots.help: The architecture with the controls in place: usually started from the Risk and security model template.

slots.label: Reference models
slots.help: Models read for context only.

templates.finish: The Architecture Board signs off the residual risk (phase G); merge the target into the current state.

templates.name: Data architecture and governance
templates.description: When who owns which data, what it means, how good it is and where it flows must be organised: a data strategy, master data, a data catalogue, analytics, privacy and records. The data principles and roles (owner, steward, custodian), the domains in scope, the information against the capabilities, the system of record for each master entity, definitions, lineage and classification, quality rules and targets, and the forum that approves new sources and changed definitions.

slots.label: Current state
slots.help: The data and the applications that hold it today.

slots.label: Target state
slots.help: Owners, agreed master sources and rules in place: usually started from the Data governance model template.

slots.label: Reference models
slots.help: Models read for context only.

templates.finish: The data governance forum approves the domains and owners; merge the target into the current state.
